In this lesson you will learn about troubleshooting voltage regulator circuits and you will troubleshoot a faulted voltage regulator circuit.
INTRODUCTIONM
Voltage regulators maintain a constant Vout under changing input and output conditions.
Measuring the output voltage with a multimeter or oscilloscope will determine if the circuit is operating normally.
An incorrect voltage output indicates that the circuit is faulted.
Let's begin the lesson on VOLTAGE REGULATOR TROUBLESHOOTING EXPERIMENT......
LESSON MENU
VOLTAGE REGULATOR FAULTS
The most common faults in voltage regulators are defective semiconductor devices (transistors or zener diodes).
DISCUSSION
However, the resistors in the circuit cannot be ignored.
For the circuit to operate, all components must be functioning correctly.
Let's look at the faults in a zener diode regulator circuit first.
In this zener diode voltage regulator circuit, the input voltage and Vz set the voltage levels for Q1.
Q1 has the following voltages on its elements:
Measuring the output voltage, Ee, quickly determines if the circuit is operating correctly.
A fault in the base circuit of Q1 changes the output voltage.
If D1 opens, Q1's base voltage increases, which places Q1 into saturation. The output voltage approaches the input voltage.
R1 drops a small amount of voltage. The Transistor's base to emitter junction still operates normally dropping another .6 volts.
If R1 shorts, D1 will pull down the applied voltage to 8 V. The excessive current flow begins to damage the diode and the voltage will climb towards 12 V, eventually destroying the zener diode..
If D1 shorts, Q1's base voltage decreases, which places Q1 into cutoff. There is no output voltage.es 0 V.
The same indications are present if R1 opens. Resistance measurements determine the fault.
Faults in Q1 also change the output voltage................
A short between the collector and emitter places Ee at 12 V.

An open between the collector and base prevents collector current flow. There is still an output of 7.4 V, due to the action of the zener diode, but load current is severly reduced and there is very little voltage regulation.n...n.
A short between the base and emitter places Ee at the base voltage, .6 V higher than normal.
An open between the base and emitter prevents current flow. Vout is 0 V.
Troubleshooting zener diode voltage regulator circuits is the same as troubleshooting common base transistor circuits.

Measuring the output voltage quickly determines if the circuit is operating normally.
If the output voltage is incorrect, voltage measurements in the regulator's (Q1) base circuit will determine the fault.
This completes the information on VOLTAGE REGULATOR FAULTS...
1. Faults in voltage regulator circuits change the output voltage.
2. Measuring the output voltage quickly determines if a circuit is faulted.
3. A short is indicated by a 0 V measurement across the shorted component.
4. An open is indicated by the applied voltage being measured across the open component.
5. When the base circuit of the regulator only has two components, an open R1 or a shorted D1 is determined by resistance measurement.

Definition
At first glance, these readings indicate that R1 is shorted. The applied voltage is dropped across Q2 and D1.
However, there is another possibility. Look at the path from the output voltage (20 V) through R2 to the cathode of D1..
R2 allows current flow to D1. D1 reacts by dropping 4.7 V, normal operation of a zener diode.
Now, if Q2 were open, you would expect to measure the applied voltage across it with 0 V's across R1 and D1.
